post.summary:
`POST /api/models/unload`: llama-swap-compatible bulk unload (REQ-5) -
evict every resident non-pinned entry. Pinned residents are skipped,
never refused (the bulk form is the caller's "make room" move).

`POST /api/models/unload/{model}`: llama-swap-compatible single unload
(REQ-5). Accepts an operator alias or registry slug. Divergence from
llama-swap, deliberate: an unknown id is a 404 whose body contains the
literal `model not found` (loop-lore's classifier substring-matches it),
but a known id with nothing resident is a 200 `{"unloaded":false}` -
any 200 is an unconditional continue-case on the client, so the common
already-gone race needs no string matching at all. Pinned → 409.

get.summary:
Liveness probe. Content-negotiated: the JSON `Health` body by default
(and for `Accept: application/json`), a literal `OK` text/plain body for
probes that prefer `text/plain` (uptime monitors, `docker --health-cmd`
equivalents).

`GET /metrics`: minimal Prometheus text exposition (vLLM-vocabulary
subset; see `metrics`).

`GET /running`: llama-swap-compatible warm-set envelope (REQ-5). The
envelope key `running` and the entry key `model` are load-bearing -
loop-lore's `readRunningModels` reads only `running[].model` and
classifies any other envelope as malformed (a probe failure that leaves
the LLM resident through a `ComfyUI` render). Extra fields are additive.

post.summary: `POST /v1/artifacts`: upload one binary artifact.
post.description:
Two modes on one route:

**Single-shot** — any non-multipart body (usually
`application/octet-stream`). The whole body is the artifact; it streams
to disk (never buffered) and is rejected with a named 413
`artifact_too_large` past the configured cap. Returns `201` with the
[`ArtifactInfo`] descriptor — `id` IS the content sha256, and it is the
`{id}` of the bytes route.

**Chunked/resumable** — `multipart/form-data`. Declare `X-Chunk-Count`
on the first request; each form part is one binary chunk, optionally
tagged with an `X-Chunk-Index` header (parts without it fill the lowest
unreceived index, so chunks may arrive in any order). Every response
carries the current [`ArtifactManifest`] (`status: "uploading"` with the
received-chunk registry). To resume an interrupted upload, re-send ONLY
the missing chunks with `X-Upload-Id: <upload_id>` set (the count must
match); a duplicate chunk re-POST with identical bytes is idempotent
(`200`, no state change), while different bytes for a received index are
`409 upload_conflict`. The request delivering the last missing chunk
finalizes in-line: its manifest flips to `status: "complete"` with the
`artifact` descriptor (content sha256, size, chunk count, id). Chunks
are capped at 8 MiB each (named 413 `chunk_too_large`), the artifact
total at the configured cap (`artifact_too_large`).

Optional `X-Artifact-Content-Type` (both modes) records the content type
served by `GET /v1/artifacts/{id}/bytes` (default
`application/octet-stream`). Active types (HTML, SVG, JavaScript, XML
markup) and parameterised values are rejected. GET always forces
`Content-Disposition: attachment` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

requestBody.description: raw artifact bytes (single-shot), or multipart/form-data where each part is one binary chunk

200.description: Chunk(s) accepted; current upload manifest (complete when the final chunk landed)

400.description: Bad chunk count/index or unusable content type

409.description: Chunk index re-sent with different bytes, or chunk count changed

413.description: Chunk over 8 MiB (chunk_too_large) or artifact over the configured total cap (artifact_too_large)

500.description: No data dir (storage unavailable) or disk failure

get.summary:
`GET /v1/artifacts/{id}/bytes` (HEAD behaves identically minus the
body): stream the stored artifact from disk.
get.description:
Always answers `Accept-Ranges: bytes` and `ETag: "<sha256>"`. A single
`Range: bytes=a-b` request gets `206` + `Content-Range` + exactly the
slice; bogus/multi/unsatisfiable ranges are a named `416 invalid_range`
carrying `Content-Range: bytes */<size>`. `If-Match` with a stale `ETag`
is `412 precondition_failed`; `If-Range` with a stale `ETag` serves the
full `200` (RFC 7233). `{id}` is the content sha256 hex digest from the
upload manifest (`artifact.id`). Range responses leave this route
uncompressed — the router's compression predicate skips every response
carrying `Content-Range` — so range math and resume offsets stay honest.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Artifact id (the content sha256 hex digest) from the upload manifest

412.description: If-Match does not match the current ETag

post.summary:
`POST /v1/audio/speech` (REQ-9): `OpenAI`-shaped TTS. Same worker as
`/v1/synthesize`. `model` optional (server default TTS), `voice` passed
through; `response_format` is `"wav"` (default, RIFF/WAVE container),
`"pcm"` (raw s16le, no container), `"flac"` (lossless), or `"opus"`
(Ogg-encapsulated, gapless). Applies to every TTS backend (stub + Kokoro):
encoding runs on the worker's PCM16, never in the voice model.

400.description: Empty input, oversized input (over 4096 characters), unknown model, or unsupported response_format

post.summary:
`POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` (REQ-9): `OpenAI`-shaped multipart
wrapper over the same STT worker as `/v1/transcribe`. `file` is
required (`audio/wav`, RIFF-sniffed `application/octet-stream`, or
`audio/pcm-s16le` + `sample_rate` form field / query); `model` is
optional (server default STT); `language` optional; `response_format`
`json` (default), `verbose_json` (adds the worker's timestamped
segments), `srt` or `vtt` (`SubRip` / `WebVTT` subtitles rendered from the
same segments; `application/x-subrip` / `text/vtt`). Errors are
`OpenAI` envelopes; only a request that is not multipart at all gets
axum's transport-level 400 before the handler runs. The native route is
unchanged.

requestBody.description: multipart/form-data: file, model?, language?, response_format? (json|verbose_json|srt|vtt), sample_rate?

400.description: Missing file, bad audio, unknown model, unsupported response_format, or missing sample_rate

post.summary:
`POST /v1/audio/translations` (REQ-9 sibling; `ReviewedAudio` P1):
`OpenAI` translation shape — the multipart `file` is decoded exactly
like `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and transcribed with whisper's
**translate** task (source language auto-detected, output always
English). `model` optional (server default STT); `response_format`
`json` (default) / `verbose_json` / `srt` / `vtt`. No `language` field:
the endpoint contract fixes the OUTPUT language, and whisper's translate
task takes none. Errors are `OpenAI` envelopes, same as transcriptions.

400.description: Missing file, bad audio, unknown model, unsupported response_format, unexpected language field, or missing sample_rate

get.summary:
`GET /v1/audio/voices`: the supported TTS voice set as an OpenAI-style
list (`{object: "list", data: [{object: "voice", …}]}`). The Kokoro
backend cannot enumerate voices at runtime, so this serves the
statically documented `KOKORO_VOICES` set — honest, no model loaded,
no state. `data[].id` values are exactly what `/v1/audio/speech`
accepts as `voice`.

`GET /v1/capabilities`: the machine-readable server contract (FEAT-
capabilities-api). Everything is DERIVED at request time — compiled
features, runtime config, the live catalog snapshot, and the resource
ledger's actual admission knobs — never a prose hard-code, so the
document is always true of the process answering and `/v1/models/refresh`
or a download commit are reflected with no cache to invalidate.
get.description:
Includes `tools`, the chat tool-choice fidelity note (REQ-3): which
`tool_choice` values `/v1/chat/completions` honors verbatim vs clamps
to `auto`, and that `parallel_tool_calls` is accepted but ignored —
disclosed here instead of silently downgraded at request time.

200.description: Server capability contract (feature flags, formats, queue knobs, and the chat tool-choice fidelity note)

get.summary:
`GET /v1/catalog`: the raw catalog list, serialized from the shared
snapshot so the response is byte-identical across refreshes.

200.description: Curated catalog with local presence + fit pills

post.summary:
`POST /v1/chat`: sync worker call inside `spawn_blocking`; the residency
lease is held across the call. Only the server edge is async.

`POST /v1/chat/completions`: the `OpenAI`-compatible translation surface
(REQ-1) over the SAME pipeline, GPU lease, and swap decision as
`/v1/chat` — never an HTTP proxy. JSON body or `OpenAI` SSE
(`stream: true`). Errors are `OpenAI` envelopes; statuses: 400 bad
request, 404 unknown model, 429 busy (+`Retry-After` via the shared
middleware), 500 inference failure. Undeclared request keys (`top_p`,
`stop`, …) are accepted and ignored by serde.
post.description:
An omitted/empty `model` is a 400 naming the requirement — the native
route's empty-means-server-default fallback stays native-only.

post.summary:
`POST /v1/chat/stream`: same blocking call, tokens forwarded as SSE
(`data: {"token":"..."}` + `data: [DONE]`) over an unbounded channel so
the sink never blocks the worker thread.
post.description:
Disconnect handling: dropping the SSE body sets a cancel flag and calls
the pipeline `abort` hook; the worker notices at its **next token
boundary** — token delivery stops, the GPU residency lease is freed, and
the synchronous FFI loop exits at its next internal checkpoint (per-token
decode returns to our loop, so early return needs no FFI-level abort).

get.summary:
`GET /v1/downloads`: every known download with its progress (poll
contract; no SSE).

post.summary:
`POST /v1/downloads`: start one managed download into the configured
models root. `{repo, file, kind}` derives the `HuggingFace` resolve URL
(and enforces the LFS sha256 when the repo API publishes one); `url` is
the direct-source alternative. A second pull of the same target file
joins the in-flight download (same id); a target that already exists
resolves immediately as `done` + `already_present`.

400.description: Missing/ambiguous source, bad repo id, or unusable file name

500.description: No managed models root or target directory create failed

get.summary: `GET /v1/downloads/{id}`: one download's progress; 404 for an unknown id.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Download id from the POST acceptance body

delete.summary:
`DELETE /v1/downloads/{id}`: cancel a download (204). The task stops at
the next chunk boundary, deletes the `.part` + meta sidecar, and lands
in `cancelled`; a queued download never starts. 409 once terminal.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Download id from the POST acceptance body

post.summary:
`POST /v1/embeddings` (REQ-4): OpenAI-shaped embeddings over the same
residency model as chat — one GPU slot, `spawn_blocking` inference.
Resolution: alias/slug → 404 envelope when unknown; a model without
`capabilities.embeddings` is refused with an explicit 400 (never
loaded, never garbage tokens). The pipeline is cached per slug
(`EmbedCache`: load-once, idle-TTL reuse, capacity 1) outside the
slot; the embed call itself runs inside the lease.
post.description:
Errors: 400 bad body / not-embeddings-capable, 404 unknown model, 429
busy slot (+`Retry-After` via the shared middleware), 500 embed failure.

400.description: Bad request or not an embeddings-capable model

get.summary:
`GET /v1/events`: the registry-wide job lifecycle feed as a
Server-Sent-Events stream (observability only — it registers no job and
touches no GPU slot). Every in-flight GPU job of every kind emits:
get.description:
- `event: job_registered` — the job entered the registry (route
  admitted the request; it may still be waiting in the admission
  queue);
- `event: job_cancelled` — a cancel was REQUESTED for the job (POST
  `.../cancel` or DELETE `/v1/jobs/{id}`); not a completion event;
- `event: job_finished` — the job left the registry (its request ended,
  any outcome).

Each frame's JSON `data` mirrors the SSE `event` line in its `event`
field (`JobEvent`): `id`, `kind`, `model` (when known),
`started_at_ms`, `interruptible`, and `cancelled` (= a cancel had been
requested at that point; on `job_finished` it is `true` for a
token-marked job, which for a non-interruptible job still ran to
completion). Frames are transition-only: a subscriber that falls more
than 256 events behind gets an `events_dropped` frame naming the skipped
count (honest gap marker, never silent skipping), and (re)connecting
replays nothing — `GET /v1/jobs` is the current-state snapshot.

200.description: SSE stream of job lifecycle events (job_registered / job_cancelled / job_finished; catalogue above)

get.summary: List discovered external engines and their capabilities.

post.summary: Re-probe all external engines and refresh the capability cache.

get.summary: Probe one external tool, optionally requiring a capability.

501.description: Tool or requested capability is unavailable

post.summary:
`POST /v1/image-ops` (epic-editor-integration): one bounded CPU op over
`1..=8` inputs — resize/crop/rotate/grayscale/format — deterministic by
construction (Lanczos3, fixed encoders), with `request_id`-keyed
idempotency (same key + same canonical command replays the first job's
response byte-identically, no double execution; same key + different
command is a named 400). The job is registry-visible while live (kind
`image_ops`, cancel honored BETWEEN inputs), its lifecycle streams on
`GET /v1/events`, and the result bundle lands under
`<data_dir>/jobs/{bundle}/` via the existing jobs path (sidecar: command
hash, input/output hashes, tool version, attempts, outcome). Inputs are
data URIs or this server's own bundle artifacts only — no paths, no
`file://`, no remote URLs (nothing is fetched, so there is no SSRF
surface). Unsupported-in-principle ops do not exist in the vocabulary:
the op set is exactly what the in-process `image` crate covers
(TASK-cheap-ops-spike Tier 0), so there is no 501 path today — unknown
op tags are a 400 from parsing, and the capabilities advertisement lists
the supported vocabulary.

200.description: One output per input, in order

400.description: Unknown field, unknown op, out-of-range params, oversized batch, bad input container/data URI/ artifact, unknown output_format or output_compression, or request_id conflict

post.summary:
`POST /v1/images/edits`: pragmatic honkbox img2img/inpaint shape over
the same SD pipeline seam as `/v1/images/generations` (single image per
request, `n` fixed at 1). `image` is a required PNG (magic-sniffed; the
declared content type is not trusted), `mask` an optional PNG that
turns the run into inpainting; `prompt` is required; `strength` (the
denoise amount, `(0, 1]`, default 0.75) applies to the init image;
`size` defaults to the source image's dimensions; the remaining recipe
fields (`recipe`/`sampler`/`scheduler`/`cfg_scale`/`steps`/
`negative_prompt`/`seed`) validate exactly like `generations` — a named
recipe plus per-field overrides, explicit fields winning. `output_format`
(`png` default | `jpeg` | `webp` lossless) and `output_compression`
(JPEG quality `[0, 100]`; ignored for lossless PNG/WebP) mirror the
`generations` knobs — unknown format names and non-numeric/out-of-range
compression values are named 400s, never clamps. No
`hires_fix` on this route: the output stays at the source image's
dimensions. Inputs are staged as temp
PNG paths (the vendor reads images from the filesystem) and removed
after the generation, including on failure. `loras` (a JSON array of
`{slug, strength}` objects) resolves through the same
[`resolve_loras`] as `generations` — max 2, strength `[-2, 2]`
reject-not-clamp, catalog lookup, single directory — with license notes
surfaced as response `warnings` and the resolved slugs/strengths recorded
in the bundle sidecar. The stub
backend honestly ignores image inputs, so its pixels never depend on
the upload; tests cover the wire/validation paths. Errors are `OpenAI`
envelopes: 400 (missing image/prompt, non-PNG bytes, bad
`strength`/`size`/`recipe`/`output_format`/`output_compression`/`loras`
fields), 404
unknown model, 429 busy, 500 staging or generation failure.

requestBody.description: multipart/form-data: image (PNG, required), mask? (PNG), prompt (required), model?, strength?, size?, recipe?, sampler?, scheduler?, cfg_scale?, steps?, negative_prompt?, seed?, output_format? (png|jpeg|webp), output_compression? (JPEG quality 0-100), loras? (JSON array of {slug, strength})

200.description: Edited image (base64-encoded bytes in the requested output_format)

400.description: Missing image/prompt, non-PNG bytes, bad strength, size, recipe, output_format, output_compression, or loras fields

post.summary:
`POST /v1/images/generations` (REQ-10): the `OpenAI` image-generation
shape over the startup-configured [`SdPipeline`]. SD pipelines are
startup-static (no swap manager), so a request `model` is validated and
recorded (bundle sidecar) but the pipeline stays the one built at
startup — with the stub backend any slug is honest; with `sd-cpp` the
checkpoint is the `--sd-model` one.
post.description:
`output_format` selects the container for the returned bytes (`png`
default, `jpeg`, `webp` lossless; unknown names are a 400 naming it) and
the bundle sidecar/extension agree with it. `output_compression` is the
JPEG quality `[0, 100]`; non-numeric/out-of-range values are a named 400,
and the knob is ignored (as documented) for lossless PNG/WebP.

Each image in the request is generated under the GPU lease
(`spawn_blocking`, like every other GPU route) and written to the
existing job bundle store (`<data_dir>/jobs/`), so CLI GC and
recordkeeping cover HTTP generations too. Errors are `OpenAI`
envelopes: 400 bad `size`/`response_format`/`output_format`/
`output_compression`/recipe params (unknown
recipe/sampler/scheduler name, `cfg_scale` outside [1.0, 30.0], `steps`
outside [1, 100], invalid `hires_fix` scale/target/denoise, `LoRA` slug
/ strength / count violations), 404 unknown model, 429 busy, 500
backend failure. `n` clamps to `[1, 4]` (warn, never reject).
Per-request `loras` resolve against `ModelKind::Lora` catalog entries;
their license notes surface as response `warnings` (weights are never
bundled; ReviewedLicense-AGPL §2b/§2c). `recipe` selects a curated
sampler/scheduler/cfg/steps bundle (per-field overrides win, then
server defaults); `hires_fix` runs the vendor-native second-pass
upscale and is recorded in the bundle sidecar. A valid `controlnet` +
`control_image` pair (plus optional `controlnet_strength`) is applied by
the sd-cpp pipeline — the weights load with the model context and the
conditioning image steers the render — while backends without a
`ControlNet` branch get the named 501 instead.

200.description: Generated images (base64-encoded bytes in the requested output_format)

400.description: Bad size, response_format, output_format, output_compression, recipe, sampler, scheduler, cfg_scale, steps, hires_fix, loras, or controlnet params (pair, image, or slug)

501.description: Valid controlnet params accepted but not applicable by the sd pipeline (controlnet_unsupported)

get.summary:
`GET /v1/jobs` (NEW-3): the in-flight registry — admitted GPU requests
(running, or waiting in the admission queue), oldest first. Entries
appear when a route admits a request and vanish when it ends; this is a
liveness view, not history (see `jobs_registry`).

post.summary:
`POST /v1/jobs/blender` (FEAT-blender-job-route): admit a typed Blender
asset job. The route validates the request, resolves the mesh from the
artifact store, checks the engine contract against the probed Blender
and takes the admission lease; the work itself runs in a supervised
Blender process (`routes/blender_exec.rs`) and the outcome lands in the
job bundle (`<data_dir>/jobs/{bundle}/`).

202.description: Job admitted; the bundle id names the job directory

400.description: Malformed request, unsupported manifest or output format, out-of-range stage params, or an input digest that does not match the artifact id

404.description: The input mesh (or a texture) is not in the artifact store

409.description: The engine contract does not match the installed Blender or recipe

413.description: The input mesh is over the byte cap

501.description: No Blender engine is installed, or the host cannot supervise a process group

503.description: No data dir: the artifact store and the job bundles are disabled

delete.summary:
`DELETE /v1/jobs/{id}`: the REST-shaped spelling of
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` — deleting an in-flight job means requesting
its cooperative cancel, nothing more. Same token machinery, same honest
200 `{cancelled}` / 404 contract (see [`cancel_job_response`]); the
DELETE does not wait for the job to end and never removes finished-work
records (job bundles under `<data_dir>/jobs/` are a separate concern).

get.summary:
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}/bundle.zip`: rebuild a deterministic ZIP of the job
bundle. Missing/unreadable job directories are 404; count and byte caps
are reject-not-clamp 413s.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: 26-character Crockford ULID of the job bundle

200.description: Deterministic ZIP of the job bundle

413.description: Bundle exceeds the entry or byte caps

post.summary:
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` (NEW-3): mark the job's cooperative-stop
token. See [`cancel_job_response`] for the honest response contract.

get.summary:
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}/content/{name}`: stream one allowlisted bundle file.
Missing files are 404, oversized files are 413; nothing is buffered whole.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: 26-character Crockford ULID of the job bundle

400.description: Malformed job id or disallowed name

404.description: No such job bundle or file

get.summary:
`GET /v1/memory`: residency readout (REQ-5) - exactly the models the
swap manager considers resident, with `loaded_at`, `expires_at`,
`pinned`, and the best-effort `in_use` flag, plus the configured
capacity and the GPU slot state. Without a swap manager (stub backends)
the resident list is empty and capacity reads zeros - nothing is
managed.

`GET /v1/models`: the discovered-model catalog as an OpenAI-style list
envelope (`{object: "list", data: [...]}`). Served from the shared scan
snapshot; `POST /v1/models/refresh` re-scans and swaps it.

post.summary:
`POST /v1/models/refresh`: re-scan the configured registry roots and
swap the shared catalog snapshot, returning the fresh body. Idempotent;
missing or unreadable roots never fail the request (the scan is lenient —
they contribute empty results). Root *configuration* still needs a
restart; refresh picks up files added under the configured roots.

delete.summary:
`DELETE /v1/models/{slug}` (`NewItems` §1): explicit, **permanent** model
deletion — the weight file (or directory) is removed from disk and the
catalog entry is dropped; there is no trash and no undo, recovery means
downloading the model again. Guardrails: an unknown slug (alias or
registry slug) is a 404; a resident or busy model (chat warm-set
residency: resident, pinned, or in-flight) is refused with 409 — unload
it first (`POST /v1/models/{slug}/unload`). Success removes the file(s),
re-scans the registry roots (best-effort SQLite cache sync) and drops
the entry from the shared catalog snapshot, then returns 200 naming
exactly what was removed.

409.description: Model is resident, pinned, or busy; unload it first

post.summary:
`POST /v1/models/{slug}/unload`: explicitly evict one resident model
(REQ-5). Accepts an operator alias or the registry slug. A resident
non-pinned entry is evicted (`{"unloaded":true,"reason":"explicit"}`);
a non-resident or unknown id is an idempotent 200
(`{"unloaded":false,"reason":"not_loaded"}`); a pinned resident is
refused with 409 and a loud log. In-flight requests are never aborted:
eviction only drops the cache's own `Arc` handle.

`POST /v1/recognize` (recognition tickets): one image in, recognition
out. Stage 1 is synchronous — barcode-class latency is sub-millisecond,
so the request-response shape needs no job registry entry; the
OCR/document pipeline becomes job-based (cancellable, cache-keyed per
FEAT-ocr-ingest) when the first OCR backend lands, and this route is
that shape's already-valid request prefix. Only `data:` URI image
payloads are accepted: nothing is ever fetched, so there is no SSRF
surface (same policy as `/v1/image-ops`). Kinds without a compiled
backend answer the named 501 `recognition_kind_unsupported` — the same
`kinds()` gate the top-level `recognition` capability advertises, so
honest absence is observable from both directions.

200.description: Recognition result (`pages: []` when a valid image held nothing recognizable)

400.description: Unknown field or kind (typed enum parse), non-`data:` URI, undeclared base64, unsupported container, invalid base64, or empty payload

501.description: Kind (or engine override) not served by this build's compiled backends (`recognition_kind_unsupported`)

post.summary: `POST /v1/synthesize`: JSON in, WAV bytes out (`audio/wav`).

400.description: Unknown model slug; blank `text`; `text` over the 4096-character cap (`text_too_long`)

post.summary:
`POST /v1/transcribe`: content-type dispatch (`audio/wav` → `decode_wav`,
`audio/pcm-s16le` → raw LE bytes + required `?sample_rate=`), then the
sync worker call inside `spawn_blocking`.

400.description: Unknown model, bad audio, or missing sample_rate

ArtifactChunk.description:
One received chunk record in an artifact upload manifest
(`POST /v1/artifacts` chunked mode).

sha256.description: sha256 digest (lowercase hex) of this chunk's bytes.

ArtifactInfo.description:
Completed artifact descriptor: `id` is the content sha256 hex digest and
doubles as the `{id}` of `GET /v1/artifacts/{id}/bytes`.

chunk_count.description: Number of chunks the artifact was uploaded in (1 for single-shot).

content_type.description:
Content type served by the bytes route (default
`application/octet-stream`).

id.description: Content sha256 (lowercase hex) — the artifact id.

sha256.description: Same digest, named explicitly for direct hash checks.

ArtifactManifest.description:
Upload manifest returned on every chunked `POST /v1/artifacts` request:
the registry of received chunks plus the completed artifact descriptor
once the final chunk lands.

oneOf.description:
Absent until the upload completes; present exactly when `status` is
`"complete"`.

received.description: Received chunk indices, ascending (the resume worklist's complement).

upload_id.description: Server-assigned upload session id (`X-Upload-Id` on resume).

mode.description:
`"none"` (loopback-only operation) or `"bearer"` (key required on
every route except the probes). The key VALUE is never in this
document.

BlenderBakeMap.description: The maps a bake can produce.

BlenderEngine.description:
The engine contract a Blender job expects. Both fields are checked
against the installed engine before the process starts.

blender_version.description: The Blender version the caller expects (e.g. `"4.5.15"`).

script_version.description:
The recipe content pin: the sha256 of the embedded recipe BYTES
(`recipe_sha256()`, 64 lowercase hex). Absent = the caller pins no
recipe (the server runs its current one); present = the digest must
match, so a recipe change is a named 409
(`blender_script_version_mismatch`) instead of a silently different
result. This is a CONTENT digest only: a digest of a script path (or
of any other string) can never match and is rejected the same way.
A caller that cannot compute the byte digest omits the field.

bundle.description:
Bundle id (ULID) under `<data_dir>/jobs/{bundle}/` — the manifest and
the artifacts land there. Absent when the server runs without a data
dir (bundles are disabled).

job_id.description:
Registry job id (`job_<ulid>`); matches `GET /v1/jobs`, the
`X-Job-Id` header and the cancel route while the job is live.

independent of the crate version. Bump it when the contract changes

ops.description: Supported op wire names (the `ImageOpCommand` tag vocabulary).

ImagesGenerationRequest.description:
`POST /v1/images/generations` request (REQ-10). `OpenAI` shape: `prompt`
required; `model` optional (server default SD pipeline); `size` is
`"WxH"` pixels (default `1024x1024`, longest edge capped by sd-core);
`n` defaults to 1 and is clamped (never rejected) to 4;
`response_format` currently only accepts `"b64_json"`.

Recipe overrides (all optional; omitting every one is byte-identical to
the pre-passthrough fixed recipe: euler sampler, `normal`/discrete
scheduler, CFG 7.0, server-chosen seed base):
- `sampler`: one of the sd.cpp sampler names; an unknown name is a 400
  naming it (accepted list comes from sd-core `SAMPLER_NAMES`).
- `scheduler`: one of the sd.cpp scheduler names; unknown name = 400.
- `cfg_scale`: classifier-free guidance scale in `[1.0, 30.0]`; outside
  the range is a 400 (rejected, never silently clamped).
- `negative_prompt`: text steered away from in CFG models.
- `seed`: RNG base; per-image seed = `seed + i`. Omitted = the
  server-chosen fixed base (deterministic, like today).
- `loras`: per-request `LoRA` adapters (max 2; each `slug` resolves
  against catalog entries of kind `lora` by slug or alias — unknown
  names are a 400 naming the offender). `strength` is the adapter
  multiplier, default 1.0, accepted range `[-2.0, 2.0]` (out of range
  is a 400, never clamped). Weight licensing is the operator's
  responsibility: honkbox never bundles `LoRA` weights, and the curated
  catalog `license` is surfaced as a response warning when known — a
  missing license means all-rights-reserved, i.e. local-only use
  (ReviewedLicense-AGPL §2b/§2c). The high-noise adapter split is not
  exposed; requests always apply adapters as standard `LoRA`s. Base-model
  mismatch cannot be detected today (no base tags are recorded on scan
  entries or `LoRA` files), so it is neither warned about nor rejected.

**Named recipes and precedence**: `recipe` selects a curated bundle
(sampler/scheduler/cfg/steps for a checkpoint family; names come from
sd-core's supported enums and mirror the vendored stable-diffusion.cpp
presets — e.g. `sd15`, `sdxl`, `sd35`, `turbo`, `lcm`, `flux-dev`,
`flux-schnell`; an unknown name is a 400 listing every accepted value).
Explicit per-field overrides ALWAYS win over the recipe defaults, which
in turn win over the server defaults: request field > recipe > server
default. Omitting `recipe` and every override field reproduces the
pre-recipe fixed recipe exactly (euler, discrete, CFG 7.0, 20 steps).
The applied recipe name — and which fields a recipe actually supplied —
land verbatim in the job bundle sidecar.

cfg_scale.description:
Classifier-free guidance scale; accepted range `[1.0, 30.0]`, values
outside it are rejected with a 400 (never silently clamped).

control_image.description:

base64-encoded PNG. Validated (bad base64 / not a PNG = 400) and
applied as-is by the sd-cpp pipeline — pass a preprocessed
conditioning map (depth, edges, pose); the engine resizes it to the
generation size.

conditioning image depicts — one of the engine's names or aliases
(`none`, `openpose`, `depth`, `scribble`, `canny`, `normal`,
`segment`, `tile`, `repaint`, plus engine aliases like `lineart`,
`hed`, `mlsd`). Validated against the engine's own name table
(unknown names are a 400 `unknown_control_type`); a union
`ControlNet` requires a named type while a classic one accepts the
default `none` (omitted = `none`, the preprocessed-map behavior).
Only meaningful with `controlnet` + `control_image`.

(honkbox extension, not part of the `OpenAI` image shape). Accepted
and validated (unknown slug = 400) together with
[`ImagesGenerationRequest::control_image`]; a fully valid pair is
applied by the sd-cpp pipeline (weights load with the model
context, the conditioning image steers the render). A pipeline that
cannot apply control inputs (the stub backend) is answered with an
explicit 501 (`controlnet_unsupported`), never silently ignored.

controlnet_strength.description:
`ControlNet` guidance strength in `(0, 1]` (how hard the conditioning
image steers the render); values outside the range are rejected with
a 400 (`invalid_controlnet_strength`), never clamped. Omitted = the
vendor default 0.9 (stable-diffusion.cpp `--control-strength`).
Only meaningful with `controlnet` + `control_image`.

Optional hires-fix second pass: generate at `size`, interpolate the
latent up to the target, re-denoise (see [`ImagesHiresFix`]).

loras.description:
Per-request `LoRA` adapters (see the struct-level docs for the
licensing and validation rules); omit = plain checkpoint render.

model.description:
Model id (alias or registry slug) from the SD catalog; omitted →
the startup-configured SD pipeline (`--sd-model`, stub default).

n.description:
Number of images (1-4; above 4 is clamped down with a warn, never a
400 — the same clamp-not-reject policy as `ttl_seconds`).

output_compression.description:
JPEG quality in `[0, 100]` (the `OpenAI` `output_compression`
precedent). Only meaningful with `output_format: "jpeg"` — PNG is
lossless and WebP is encoded lossless-only today, so the value is
documented-and-ignored there. Non-integer or out-of-range values are
rejected with a 400 (`invalid_output_compression`), never clamped.
Omitted = JPEG quality 90.

output_format.description:
Output container for the returned image bytes: `"png"` (default),
`"jpeg"`, or `"webp"` (lossless). Unknown names are rejected with a
400 listing the accepted values. The `response_format` transport
encoding stays `"b64_json"` either way.

recipe.description:
Named generation recipe (curated sampler/scheduler/cfg/steps bundle
per checkpoint family); unknown names are rejected with a 400 listing
every accepted value. Explicit per-field overrides win over recipe
defaults (see the struct-level precedence docs).

sampler.description:
Sampler override (sd.cpp name, e.g. `"euler"`, `"dpm++2m"`);
unknown names are rejected with a 400 listing the accepted values.

scheduler.description:
Scheduler override (sd.cpp name, e.g. `"discrete"`, `"karras"`);
unknown names are rejected with a 400 listing the accepted values.

seed.description:
RNG seed base; per-image seed = `seed + i`. Omitted = the fixed
server-chosen base (deterministic across identical requests).

steps.description:
Diffusion steps override; accepted range `[1, 100]`, outside it is a
400 (rejected, never clamped). Omitted = the recipe default, else the
server default of 20.

`POST /v1/images/generations` response: Unix `created` seconds plus one
`data` entry per requested image (`n`).

data.description: One entry per requested image, in order.

warnings.description: Advisory notes (`LoRA` license surfacing); omitted when empty.

ImagesHiresFix.description:
Optional hires-fix second pass on [`ImagesGenerationRequest::hires_fix`].
Vendor-native two-pass upscale (stable-diffusion.cpp `sd_hires_params_t`,
latent upscaler): the image is generated at the requested `size`, the
latent is interpolated up to the target, and a second pass re-denoises at
`denoise`. `target` wins over `scale`. The final edge stays under the
same 2048 px cap as plain generation; violations are a 400.

scale.description:
Upscale factor over the requested `size`; accepted range
`[1.0, 4.0]`, default 2.0.

target.description:
Explicit target size `"WxH"` (e.g. `"2048x1152"`); overrides
`scale` when present.

slug.description:
Catalog slug or alias of a `lora`-kind entry (e.g.
`comfy:loras/detail.safetensors`); unknown names are a 400.

JobCancelResult.description:
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` response (NEW-3). `cancelled` is `true`
when a cancel was requested for a found id — the cooperative-stop token
was marked — and is never `false` for a found id; an unknown id
(finished or never registered) is a plain-text 404. Whether the work can
actually stop early is a SEPARATE fact: `interruptible` is reported per
job by [`JobInfo`] (`GET /v1/jobs`) and by the `job_cancelled`
[`JobEvent`] (`GET /v1/events`), not by this response.

cancelled.description:
`true` = a cancel was requested and the token was marked (every
found id); `false` is never returned here — an unknown id is a 404.
Does NOT say whether the job can stop early; read `interruptible`
from [`JobInfo`] or the `job_cancelled` [`JobEvent`].

JobEvent.description:
One job lifecycle event streamed by `GET /v1/events`. The registry is a
liveness view, so events are transitional: no history is replayed on
(re)connect — a fresh stream only sees jobs registered after it opened.

cancelled.description:
Whether a cancel had been requested for the job at the event's
point in time: always `true` on `job_cancelled`, `false` on
`job_registered`, and on `job_finished` `true` means the token was
marked before the job ended — for a non-interruptible job that
still means the work ran to completion.

event.description:
Lifecycle transition (also carried as the SSE `event:` line so
JSON-only consumers do not need the envelope).

interruptible.description:
Whether the job checks its cancel token between work units (same
contract as [`JobInfo::interruptible`]).

model.description: Model slug the job runs against, when known.

started_at_ms.description:
Registration time, Unix milliseconds (same value `GET /v1/jobs`
reports for the live entry).

JobEventType.description:
Which lifecycle transition a [`JobEvent`] carries (`GET /v1/events`
SSE frames; the wire labels double as the SSE `event:` line).

JobInfo.description:
One in-flight GPU job of `GET /v1/jobs` (NEW-3). Entries appear when a
GPU route admits a request and vanish when the request ends — this is a
liveness view, not history.

id.description:
Registry id (`job_<ulid>`); pass to `POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel`.
Also stamped as the `X-Job-Id` response header of the owning request
(on SSE routes it precedes the stream body).

interruptible.description:
Whether the job checks its cancel token between work units:
`true` = a cancel stops it at the next checkpoint (multi-image
generations between images, streaming chat at the next token);
`false` = the single blocking FFI call cannot be interrupted and
runs to completion (engine-level cancellation needs a per-backend
spike, per the design record).

model.description: Model slug the job runs against, when known.

JobList.description:
`GET /v1/jobs` response: OpenAI-style list envelope over in-flight GPU
jobs, oldest first.

name.description: Schema name (`OpenAI` requires one; only echoed, never enforced).

schema.description:
The JSON Schema itself; converted to a GBNF grammar on the llama.cpp
path.

strict.description:
`OpenAI` strict-mode flag; accepted (grammar enforcement is always
strict here).

slot_busy.description: Another job currently holds the single inference slot.

MemoryInfo.description:
Residency readout (`GET /v1/memory`): exactly the models the swap
manager considers resident, plus configured capacity and GPU state.

bytes_reserved.description:
Sum of the resident entries' estimated bytes (REQ-12); an
**estimate** (registry on-disk weight sizes), never a measurement.
Absent when no resident entry has a known estimate (or the swap
manager is off).

ModelCapabilities.description:
Feature flags for one model (`GET /v1/models` entry `capabilities`).

Defaults derive from the entry's `kind` (see [`ModelCapabilities::for_kind`]);
an operator `[[models.entry]]` capabilities declaration overrides
individual flags. Emitted as a nested object for OpenAI/llama-swap-style
consumers — loop-lore reads the same values off the entry root as flat
fields, which are emitted alongside (`tool_calling`, `modalities`, …).

chat.description: Chat-template conversation turns (an LLM pipeline can serve it).

completion.description: Raw completion; mirrors `chat` (honkbox loads whole turns either way).

embeddings.description: Embedding vectors (e.g. an operator-declared embedding GGUF).

ModelCatalogEntry.description:
One discovered model in the catalog (`GET /v1/models`).

`id` is the operator alias when one is configured for the file, else the
registry slug; requests accept either (the raw slug always works, via
`slug`). The loop-lore flat fields (`owned_by`, `context_length`,
`max_output`, `thinking`, `tool_calling`, `modalities`) mirror the nested
`capabilities` object so both consumer shapes work.

capabilities.description: Feature flags (also mirrored into the flat fields above).

category.description: Directory category (`checkpoints`, `loras`, LLM parent dir, or `root`).

context_length.description: Training context length from GGUF metadata; `null` when unprobed.

id.description: Operator alias when configured, else the registry slug.

kind.description:
Modality (capability overrides may reclassify a root, e.g. an
operator-declared embedding GGUF under an LLM root).

max_output.description: Generation cap; `null` (honkbox has no per-model output ceiling).

oneOf.description:
Header-derived metadata (GGUF/safetensors); absent when the file has
no probeable header or the header is invalid.

owned_by.description: Ownership label; local files are always `"local"`.

path.description: Absolute path to the weight file.

slug.description: Registry slug (`llm:…` / `comfy:…`), always present regardless of `id`.

thinking.description: Reasoning/thinking support (no honkbox model declares it today).

ModelDeleteResult.description:
Explicit model deletion result (`DELETE /v1/models/{slug}`). Deletion
is **permanent**: the weight file(s) are removed from disk and the
catalog entry is dropped; recovery means downloading again.

slug.description: Registry slug the request resolved to.

ModelKind.description:
Model modality as discovered on disk (`GET /v1/models` entries). Mirrors
the registry's on-disk kinds.

oneOf.description: `.gguf`: llama.cpp container header.
`.safetensors`: `HuggingFace` container header.

ModelMetadata.description: Optional on-disk header metadata, tagged by container format.

name.description: Tool name to steer the model towards.

model.description:
The resolved model's served id (alias when bound, else the slug);
the server-default path echoes the request value.

OpenAiChatRequest.description:
OpenAI-compatible chat completion request (`POST /v1/chat/completions`;
REQ-1). A translation surface over honkbox's native chat pipeline — the
request is served by the same pipeline, GPU lease, and swap decision as
`POST /v1/chat`.

Undeclared keys (`top_p`, `stop`, `reasoning_budget`, `cache_prompt`, …)
are accepted and silently ignored (serde's default unknown-key behavior);
only the fields below have honkbox-side meaning.

REQ-3 additions and their fidelity:
- **Enforced** (never silently ignored): `tools` + `tool_calls`,
  `response_format` (`json_object`/`json_schema` → GBNF grammar), raw
  `grammar` (llama.cpp GBNF, honored verbatim), `tool_choice: "none"`.
  `tools` combined with `grammar`/`response_format` is a 400 (mutually
  exclusive constraint), matching llama.cpp's own hard error.
- **Clamped, disclosed**: `tool_choice` `"required"`/`"any"`/named
  function all behave as `"auto"` (tools offered, model decides) —
  accepted, never a 400; the clamp is published machine-readably on
  `GET /v1/capabilities` (`tools`), so the contract is visible before
  the client sends.
- **Accepted and ignored, disclosed**: `parallel_tool_calls` — one tool
  call is produced per turn regardless; the field exists so clients
  that always send it are not rejected. `capabilities.tools.
  parallel_tool_calls = false` says so up front.
- **Extended sampler params, wired into the sampler chain**: `top_k`,
  `min_p`, `typical_p`, `repeat_penalty`, `xtc_probability`,
  `dry_multiplier`/`dry_base`/`dry_allowed_length`,
  `dynatemp_range`/`dynatemp_exponent`. All are supported by the
  llama-cpp-4 binding; each is applied only when present.

dry_allowed_length.description:
DRY sequence length below which no penalty applies (llama.cpp
default 2). Wired when `dry_multiplier` is present.

dry_base.description:
DRY penalty exponent base (llama.cpp default 1.75). Wired when
`dry_multiplier` is present.

dry_multiplier.description: DRY repetition penalty strength (0 = off). Wired when present.

dynatemp_exponent.description:
Dynamic temperature exponent (llama.cpp default 1.0). Wired when
`dynatemp_range` is present.

dynatemp_range.description: Dynamic temperature range (0 = off). Wired when present.

grammar.description:
Raw GBNF grammar (llama.cpp `grammar` field), honored verbatim as
the sampler chain's head. An unparseable grammar is a 400.

max_tokens.description: Max tokens to generate; backend default when absent.

min_p.description:
Minimum probability for a token to be kept (llama.cpp `min_p`).
Wired when present.

model.description:
Model id: an operator alias or registry slug (`GET /v1/models`).
Required on this route — an omitted/empty model is a 400 naming the
requirement (the native route's empty-means-server-default fallback
stays native-only).

parallel_tool_calls.description:
Accepted and ignored (disclosed: `capabilities.tools.
parallel_tool_calls` is `false`): honkbox produces at most one tool
call per turn. Present so parallel-`true` clients are not rejected.

repeat_penalty.description:
Repetition penalty (llama.cpp `repeat_penalty`; 1.0 = off). Wired
when present.

oneOf.description:
Structured output (`REQ-3`): `json_object` → any-JSON grammar,
`json_schema` → schema converted to GBNF. Both enforced on the
llama.cpp path, never a silently unconstrained string.

seed.description:
Deterministic sampling seed, honored end-to-end (sampler chain): the
same prompt + seed streams the same tokens the non-streaming path
returns.

stream.description:
Stream `OpenAI` SSE chunks (`chat.completion.chunk` frames + a final
`data: [DONE]` line) instead of one JSON body. Default false.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature; backend default when absent.

oneOf.description:
`"auto"` / `"none"` / `"required"` / named. Only `"none"` changes
behavior; everything else is clamped to `auto` (accepted, never a
400 — see `capabilities.tools` on `GET /v1/capabilities` for the
machine-readable honored/clamped vocabulary).

tools.description:
`OpenAI` tool definitions (`REQ-3`). Non-empty arrays switch the
worker onto the tool-capable chat template: the model's tool-call
grammar constrains generation and tool calls are parsed from the
output (`finish_reason: "tool_calls"`).

top_k.description:
Distinct tokens considered per step (llama.cpp `top_k`; `<= 0`
disables). Wired when present.

ttl_seconds.description:
Per-request residency advice; identical contract to
[`ChatRequest::ttl_seconds`].

typical_p.description:
Locally-typical sampling mass (llama.cpp `typical_p`). Wired when
present.

xtc_probability.description:
Probability of excising the top token when a close runner-up exists
(llama.cpp `xtc_probability`; 0 = off). Wired when present.

OpenAiChunk.description:
Streaming chunk (`object: "chat.completion.chunk"`). `usage` rides only
on the final frame.

id.description: `chatcmpl-<ulid>`, shared by every frame of one completion.

oneOf.description: Token accounting; present only on the final frame.

OpenAiChunkChoice.description: One streamed chunk choice (`choices[]` of a chunk).

oneOf.description: `null` on every frame except the last.

OpenAiDelta.description:
One streamed delta (`choices[].delta` of a chunk). All fields optional:
the first frame carries `role`, token frames carry `content`, tool-call
frames carry `tool_calls` (`REQ-3`), the final frame carries none.

content.description: Next text piece, token frames only.

oneOf.description: Assistant role marker, first frame only.

tool_calls.description:
Tool-call fragments (`REQ-3`): the first frame of a call carries
`id`/`type`/`name` + empty `arguments`, later frames append to
`arguments` at the same `index`. Concatenating the `arguments`
fragments per index yields the complete JSON string.

prompt_tokens.description:
Prompt tokens after tokenization (real count on the llama.cpp path;
the stub reports 0).

compression.description:
`true` when `output_compression` affects this container (JPEG
quality only; PNG is deterministic and WebP encodes lossless-only).

Pill.description:
Fit-pill verdict for a curated catalog entry against the configured
`[models] vram_budget_bytes`. Estimates are advisory heuristics (per-kind
overhead factors over weight bytes), never a measurement.

QueueCapabilities.description:
Resource-ledger admission knobs (`Capabilities::queue`), read live from
the ledger + admission config — the same values the 429 contract uses.

gpu_slots.description: Shared GPU slots the ledger admits against.

kinds.description:
One row per admission kind (fixed vocabulary), with its bounded
queue length and TTL — a client can size its own retry cadence.

retry_after_secs.description: The `Retry-After` hint (seconds) the server's 429 responses carry.

kind.description:
Fixed kind label (`sd`, `llm`, `ocr`, `embed`, `rag`, `comfy`,
`blender`, `3d`) — never user data.

queue_cap.description: Bounded queue length for the kind.

reserved.description:
The kind is RESERVED: the ledger carries capacity for it, but no
route admits a job of that kind — the row is capacity only, never a
callable job kind. Additive field: `api_version` is unchanged (a
reserved row hides a job class, it does not change one).

ttl_secs.description:
Queue TTL in seconds (a waiter un-admitted after this long is
evicted); `0` = never expires.

RecKind.description:
Recognition surface kind (`POST /v1/recognize`, recognition tickets).
Snake-case wire names are the worker crate's `RecKind::as_str` spellings.

RecognitionEngineMeta.description: Which engine produced a result, and what its output honestly contains.

bbox_support.description:
`true` only when `regions[].bbox` carries real coordinates — a
client must not treat regions as located otherwise (VLM rule).

version.description:
Engine dependency version this build linked; absent when unknown
(the stub has none).

RecognitionFeature.description:
Recognition capability (`Capabilities::recognition`): probe-driven flags
per kind — a `true` here is the same compile probe the route's 501/200
behavior keys on, so the document cannot drift from the binary.

barcode.description: Barcode/QR decode is compiled and served by `POST /v1/recognize`.

ocr.description:
OCR is compiled and served. Always `false` until the first OCR
backend lands — honest absence, never a half seam.

RecognitionPage.description: One page of recognition output; barcode decode yields exactly one.

regions.description:
Located regions; empty when the engine cannot localize or nothing
was found.

RecognitionRegion.description:
One located region: axis-aligned pixel bbox + text. `confidence` is
absent when the engine produces none (rxing does not).

bbox.description:
Pixel bbox `[x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max]` in source-image
coordinates; meaningful only when the engine's `bbox_support` is
`true`.

confidence.description: Engine confidence in `0.0..=1.0`, absent when unknown.

text.description: Recognized text for this region (barcode: the full payload).

RecognizeRequest.description:
One recognition request over one image (`POST /v1/recognize`).

Stage 1 is synchronous: barcode-class latency is sub-millisecond. The
OCR/document pipeline becomes job-based when FEAT-ocr-ingest lands; the
request shape is its already-compatible prefix.

engine.description:
Optional engine override (`"rxing"`, `"vlm-mtmd"`, …); `None` = the
server's default backend for the kind. Unknown engines answer the
named 501 naming the engine.

image.description:
One image as a data URI (`data:image/png;base64,…`) — no paths, no
URLs, nothing is ever fetched (no SSRF surface, same policy as
`/v1/image-ops`).

language.description: Language hint (BCP-47); barcode decode ignores it.

mode.description:
Mode hint (`text_layer` | `layout_regions` | `full_page` |
`replace_text_layer`); barcode decode ignores it. Unparsed beyond
presence in stage 1 — the OCR ticket owns the vocabulary.

RecognizeResult.description:
Recognition result. `pages: []` is the honest "processed, found
nothing" answer — never an error for a valid image.

ResidentModel.description:
One resident entry of the swap manager (`GET /v1/memory`, `GET
/running`).

alias.description:
Served alias when the operator bound one, else absent (the raw slug
is always a valid request id).

bytes.description:
Estimated resident weight size in bytes, taken from the registry
scan's `bytes` for the slug (REQ-12). An **estimate** (on-disk
weight file size), never a measurement; absent when the catalog no
longer holds the slug (e.g. a re-scan removed it while resident).

expires_at.description:
Idle-window end, Unix seconds; `null` for pinned entries (they have
no TTL budget).

in_use.description:
Best-effort: another holder than the manager owns the pipeline `Arc`
right now (an in-flight request).

kind.description:
Catalog kind string (currently always `"llm"` - the swap manager's
only modality).

ResponseFormat.description:
`OpenAI` `response_format` (`REQ-3`). `json_object` and `json_schema` are
**enforced**: the schema (or a generic any-JSON grammar for
`json_object`) is converted to GBNF and wired into the sampler chain, so
the model cannot emit a non-conforming string.

oneOf.description: Required when `format_type` is `json_schema`.

RunningModel.description:
One llama-swap-compat running entry (`GET /running`). The envelope key
`running` and this entry's `model` key are load-bearing: loop-lore's
`readRunningModels` reads only `running[].model` and classifies any
other envelope as malformed.

model.description: Owning registry slug (llama-swap reports its model id here).

ttl_secs.description: Remaining idle-window seconds; `null` for pinned entries.

tensor_count.description: Tensor entries in the JSON header (`__metadata__` excluded).

version.description:
Crate version, from `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` (release version, NOT the
wire-contract version).

SpeechRequest.description:
`POST /v1/audio/speech` request (REQ-9). `model` is optional (server
default TTS); `response_format` accepts `wav` (default, RIFF/WAVE
container), `pcm` (raw little-endian signed 16-bit mono samples,
matching the `OpenAI` pcm semantics — no container, no header), `flac`
(lossless FLAC), or `opus` (Ogg-encapsulated gapless Opus); anything
else is an explicit 400.

model.description: Model id (alias or registry slug); omitted → server default TTS.

response_format.description:
Output format: `wav` (default), `pcm` (raw s16le, no container),
`flac` (lossless), or `opus` (Ogg-encapsulated, gapless).

voice.description:
Voice name; passed through to the TTS worker (Kokoro voice or
backend default).

model.description: Model id (informational; the backend is chosen by the server).

sample_rate.description: Output sample rate in Hz; backend default when absent.

ttl_seconds.description:
Per-request residency budget for this model's swap entry, in seconds
(NEW-8; same contract as [`ChatRequest::ttl_seconds`]). Over-cap
values are clamped at the route; audio pipelines are startup-loaded
today, so the advice takes effect once per-kind swap lands.

voice.description: Voice name; backend default when absent.

ToolCall.description:
One tool call as it appears on an assistant message (`REQ-3`).
`arguments` is a JSON-encoded **string**, exactly as `OpenAI` clients
exchange it.

id.description:
Call id (unique per response on replies; echoed by `role: "tool"`
messages as `tool_call_id`).

ToolCallType.description: Flavor of a tool call. Only `OpenAI` function calls are supported.

ToolCallingCapability.description:
Chat tool-calling fidelity (`Capabilities::tools`; REQ-3): the exact
`tool_choice` / `parallel_tool_calls` contract of the `OpenAI` chat
routes, published machine-readably so no request is silently downgraded
— a client can read the clamp and the ignored flag before it sends.
`tool_choice_honored` is exhaustive (`"none"` is the only mode that
changes generation); `tool_choice_clamped` lists the standard `OpenAI`
modes and is NOT exhaustive: this is an untagged string field, so any
other unrecognized value is accepted and behaves as `"auto"` too.

parallel_tool_calls.description:
`true` when `parallel_tool_calls` is honored. `false` today: at most
one tool call is produced per turn; the field is still accepted so
parallel-`true` clients are not rejected.

tool_choice_clamped.description:
`tool_choice` string modes accepted but clamped to `"auto"`
behavior ([`ToolChoiceSpec::CLAMPED_MODES`]); never a 400. Not
exhaustive: any unrecognized value is accepted and behaves as
`"auto"` too. The named-function form clamps the same way.

tool_choice_named_function_clamped.description:
The named-function form (`{"type":"function","function":{"name":…}}`)
is accepted too — and likewise clamped to `"auto"` behavior.

oneOf.description: `"auto"`, `"none"`, `"required"`, or `"any"`.
`{"type":"function","function":{"name":…}}`.

ToolChoiceSpec.description:
`OpenAI` `tool_choice` (`REQ-3`): a mode string or a named function.
Everything except `"none"` is clamped to `auto` behavior (tools are
offered; the model decides) — no rejection. The clamp is disclosed, not
silent: [`Capabilities::tools`] publishes the exact honored/clamped
vocabulary machine-readably before the client sends.

ToolType.description: Flavor of a tool definition. Only `OpenAI` function tools are supported.

end_ms.description: Segment end, milliseconds from the audio start.

start_ms.description: Segment start, milliseconds from the audio start.

TranscriptionVerbose.description:
`POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` verbose shape
(`response_format = "verbose_json"`; REQ-9): the transcript plus the
STT worker's timestamped segments (millisecond integers, honkbox
segment shape).

segments.description: Timestamped segments from the STT worker.

UnloadAllResult.description:
Bulk unload result (`POST /api/models/unload`): every non-pinned
resident was evicted; pinned residents are skipped, never refused here.

UnloadResult.description:
Explicit unload result (`POST /v1/models/{{slug}}/unload`,
`POST /api/models/unload/{{model}}`). `reason` is `"explicit"` when a
resident entry was evicted, `"not_loaded"` for an idempotent no-op (a
200, never a 404 - the caller treats any 200 as an unconditional
continue-case).

slug.description: The owning registry slug the request resolved to.

unloaded.description: `true` when a resident entry was evicted.

built.description:
`true` when THIS build compiles the mtmd path (`llm-vision`). A
text-only build reports `false`; scan-derived entries then never
advertise vision, and image parts on any entry whose
`capabilities.vision` is `false` get the named `vision_unsupported`
400 — the gate and `/v1/models` key on the same catalog flag, so
`models` counts exactly the entries the routes accept as
vision-capable. Operator-declared vision overrides still win over
the build probe (a real pipeline fails loudly at model load).

models.description:
Catalog entries currently advertising `capabilities.vision` (what
`/v1/models` serves and the web UI's model picker consumes).

language.description:
Language/locale tag derived from the Kokoro voice prefix
(e.g. `en-US`).

VoiceList.description:
`GET /v1/audio/voices` response: OpenAI-style list envelope over the
statically documented Kokoro voice set (the backend cannot enumerate
voices at runtime, so this is the *supported* set — served without any
model loaded).
